thread:
sam: Quick summary — I ran the allocator GC knob sweep across the 8-GPU test pool this morning. Seeing clear fragmentation win when we tune for small-slab reuse, but some perf tradeoffs.

marta: nice, what knobs did you change?

sam: baseline settings were default: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=32, garbage_collection_threshold=0.3.

sam: sweep changed to: expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=8, garbage_collection_threshold=0.55 (held for 30m windows).

li: can you paste the config snippet you used?

sam: sure:

```
allocator:
  expandable_segments: false
  max_split_size_mb: 8
  garbage_collection_threshold: 0.55
  gc_interval_seconds: 60
```

raj: what workload? kv-cache warmup or steady infer?

sam: mixed. 60% streaming Chat (short seq), 40% multi-turn with KV-cache growth. Warmup spike was the main pain point.

ana: results? OOMs / latency / p50?

sam: before: sporadic OOMs on node types p4d-24 (roughly 3.2% of runs flagged with transient OOM + manual restarts). After: OOMs dropped to 0.8% over same time window.

sam: fragmentation metric (heap fragmentation ratio) moved: median 0.42 -> 0.28. Peak RSS tails reduced ~18%.

marta: any latency hit?

sam: p50 generation increased ~+2ms for short requests, p99 unchanged. CPU overhead of GC slightly up, but within SLO.

li: profiling evidence? nvprof / ATen allocator traces?

sam: attached dump in #artifacts (ping me if you need access). Short summary: allocator free/alloc churn was dominated by many 1-8MB allocations during KV-cache prefills. With expandable_segments=true those became lots of small fragments; disabling it forces larger contiguous allocations and encourages reuse.

raj: odd — I'd expect expandable_segments to reduce fragmentation by allowing splits. Did it regrow too many small free segments?

sam: exactly. With our batching heuristics the runtime frequently allocated then freed many mid-sized buffers; max_split_size_mb at 32 allowed splitting big slabs into smaller ones repeatedly, which left many tiny unusable holes. Lowering max_split_size_mb reduced split frequency.

ana: any side-effects on kernel selection or batching?

sam: we saw one regression: a canary of grouped-kernel batching that prefers more, smaller work-items saw slightly higher alloc churn; rollback of that kernel routing prevented the regression. Overall knob changes compatible with current kernel selector.

li: thought: can we add a short-lived pooled buffer for KV-cache prefill that skips allocator churn entirely?

sam: yep proposal: reserve a transient pool per-GPU that preallocs large buffers on cold-start and hands out slices. Then mark them as reused rather than free/alloc. Prototype looks trivial.

marta: would that interact poorly with garbage_collection_threshold? if we hold buffers longer we might delay GC triggering.

sam: we tuned garbage_collection_threshold to 0.55 to be conservative — we want GC to run earlier than before. Pooling + earlier GC seemed complementary in tests.

dev-bot: perf-run 3725001109 -> completed. No regressions found in 5k synthetic chat samples. :white_check_mark:

raj: next steps? I can take buffer-pool prototype and run it against the long-run soak test.

sam: awesome — can you try pool + current knob set and pool + more aggressive GC (gc_threshold=0.65) to check latency tradeoffs?

raj: will do. I'll post a shortbench results thread when done.

marta: thanks Sam — please add a short blurb to the alloc-knobs playbook with recommended defaults for customers hitting KV-cache warmup OOMs. Keep it conservative for GA.

sam: yep will add. :+1:
